reasons: The remaining question is decisive and narrower than another financial attempt: obtain four exact historical native states to resolve the independently identified state-observation gap. Source and prior local RPC observations support attempting explicit historical anchors; availability is not assumed.

A pre-start gate requires 20 GiB MemAvailable and 4 GiB free disk. Two services each retain 5 GiB RAM, 10 GiB memory-plus-swap and four CPUs. The diagnostic is capped at 4 GiB RAM, no swap and two CPUs. Maximum configured resident RAM is 14 GiB, leaving 6 GiB relative to the admission floor; the floor is not a reservation or live availability claim.

The independent timer is armed before docker start. Shared activation/readiness ends at arming plus 120 seconds. The capture phase is 60 seconds, diagnostic cgroup runtime 180 seconds. Timer at 240 seconds plus at most 1 second accuracy, 25-second stop phase and 5-second stop-post allowance gives a planned 271-second bound within 300 seconds.

The stop service kills the diagnostic cgroup and stops both containers, with an independently specified force-kill stop-post fallback. The exact unit identity, active timer and monotonic arming are observed before service launch. Commands require independent terminal and physical containment observations before timer cancellation; the executor does not claim those observations itself.

At most 60 connection-readiness requests plus 17 observation requests are permitted. Each actual HTTP request has a five-second deadline and 64 KiB body cap, no redirects, a strict loopback endpoint and a four-method read allowlist. Missing/pruned state or non-readiness RPC failures fail UNKNOWN without retrying the financial operation or substituting latest state.

Exclusive durable attempt retention consumes the sole readback attempt before arming. Existing attempt/result/unit names reject reuse. Prior 31 reservations and 9300000000000031 SPECK remain consumed; no refund, extra loan attempt or allowance transfer is proposed.
